quiz.title: Matrix Multiplication Quiz (Class 10 ICSE)
quiz.intro: Eight questions on multiplying matrices — when a product exists, the order of the answer, 2×2 products, non-commutativity and the identity matrix. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: For the product AB to exist, which condition must hold?
options: Columns of A equal rows of B
Rows of A equal rows of B
A and B have the same order
Columns of A equal columns of B
questions.explanation: AB is defined only when the number of columns of A equals the number of rows of B. The 'inner' dimensions must match.

questions.q: If A is a 2×3 matrix and B is a 3×4 matrix, what is the order of AB?
questions.explanation: The product takes the outer dimensions: rows of A (2) by columns of B (4), so AB is 2×4.

questions.q: A is 3×2 and B is 2×3. Which products are defined?
questions.explanation: AB: columns of A (2) match rows of B (2), giving 3×3. BA: columns of B (3) match rows of A (3), giving 2×2. Both exist but have different orders.
B is the 2×2 identity matrix I. Multiplying any matrix by I leaves it unchanged, so AB = A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]].

questions.q: For A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] and B = [[2, 0], [1, 3]], the top-left entry of AB is:
questions.explanation: The (1,1) entry is row 1 of A dotted with column 1 of B: (1×2) + (2×1) = 2 + 2 = 4.

questions.q: Which statement about matrix multiplication is generally TRUE?
options: AB = BA only for square matrices
AB is generally not equal to BA
AB equals BA whenever both are defined
questions.explanation: Matrix multiplication is not commutative in general: AB ≠ BA. Even when both products exist, they usually differ (and may have different orders).

questions.q: The distributive law for matrices states that A(B + C) equals:
questions.explanation: Matrix multiplication distributes over addition: A(B + C) = AB + AC, provided the orders make each product defined.
The (2,2) entry is row 2 of A dotted with column 2 of B: (0×4) + (3×0) = 0 + 0 = 0.

faq.q: When can two matrices be multiplied?
faq.a: The product AB exists only if the number of columns of A equals the number of rows of B. If A is m×n and B is n×p, then AB is defined and has order m×p. When the inner dimensions do not match, the product simply does not exist.

faq.q: How do I find the order of the product AB?
faq.a: Write the orders side by side: (m×n)(n×p). Cancel the matching inner numbers, and the outer numbers give the answer's order, m×p. For example, a 2×3 times a 3×4 gives a 2×4 matrix.

faq.q: Why is AB not the same as BA?
faq.a: Matrix multiplication is not commutative. Even when both AB and BA are defined, the entries are computed from different row-column combinations, so the results usually differ — and the two products can even have different orders. Always keep the factors in the given order.

faq.q: What does the identity matrix do in multiplication?
faq.a: The identity matrix I has 1s on its main diagonal and 0s elsewhere. Multiplying any square matrix A by I of the same order leaves it unchanged: AI = IA = A. It plays the same role for matrices that the number 1 plays for ordinary numbers.
